root_cause: The SecretProviderClass azure-reports-kv pins tenantId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000009, which is a different tenant than the one Key Vault kv-reports-prod lives in (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001). The Secrets Store CSI driver requests its token from the wrong tenant authority, Key Vault rejects it with AADSTS90002 (tenant not found), and every new pod stays in ContainerCreating because secrets-store-inline cannot mount.
evidence: secretproviderclass.yaml: azure-reports-kv sets tenantId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000009 for keyvaultName kv-reports-prod
kubectl-describe-pod.txt: FailedMount events for secrets-store-inline show AADSTS90002 tenant '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000009' not found
az-account-show.json: the signed-in tenant is 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001, matching the vault and not the SecretProviderClass
az-role-assignment-list.json: Key Vault Secrets User is correctly assigned to the workload identity on kv-reports-prod, ruling out RBAC
fix: Correct the tenantId in SecretProviderClass azure-reports-kv to the Key Vault's tenant 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 and restart the stuck pods so the CSI driver picks up the corrected SecretProviderClass.
